title: Capital budget review and Beaver Creek deferral
subtitle: Routine project classifications, a heritage permit for a pumping station, and rezonings on Columbia Street and Hawthorne Street.
overview: Council spent the day reviewing the 2023 capital budget by department. It classified projects from every department as routine, so staff can start them right after final budget approval on February 13, 2023. Council also moved three projects from non-routine to routine at staff's request: sediment pond cleaning, water main relining and Waterloo's share of the Weber Street water main work.

The most significant decision was to defer the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction to the 2024-2026 capital budget {{vote:m9}}. Council cited uncertainty over development charge revenue because of provincial Bill 23. Design work will continue with funds already released. A delegate for developers had asked Council to keep the project in 2023, saying it would bring safety improvements, active transportation links and new housing to northwest Waterloo.

In the evening, Council approved a heritage permit for a new well house at the regional pumping station on William Street East {{vote:m11}}. It also approved a rezoning for an eight-storey mixed-use building at 85-89 Columbia Street West and 300 Hemlock Street {{vote:m12}}. An informal public meeting was held on a proposed six-storey student-oriented building on Hawthorne Street, with no decision. Council also held a closed session on Ontario Land Tribunal appeals, with no public report.

decisions.item: Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction
decisions.detail: Council deferred the project from the 2023 budget to the 2024-2026 capital budget {{vote:m9}} and directed staff to continue planning and design work using funding already released.
Council classified building standards, sanitary, stormwater and water projects as routine, adding stormwater ref #538 and water ref #570 to the routine list.
Council classified engineering, planning and transportation projects as routine, adding transportation ref #670 for the Weber Street water main contribution.
Council classified community programming, facility, fire, enforcement, parks and recreation projects as routine for approval on February 13, 2023.
Council classified economic development, Indigenous initiatives and equity, and strategic initiatives projects as routine for the February 13 budget vote.

decisions.item: Heritage permit at 23 William Street East
decisions.detail: Council approved a permit to demolish the existing well houses and build a new one at the regional pumping station lands, with conditions to protect the heritage buildings during construction.

decisions.item: Columbia Street West and Hemlock Street rezoning
decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-22-16 for 85-89 Columbia Street West and 300 Hemlock Street.

debate: Supporters of deferring Beaver Creek argued that the city has little unallocated development charge reserve. The project is the largest development charge-funded one, and staff estimated Bill 23 could cut development charge revenue over five years. They called moving ahead in 2023 financially irresponsible without certainty, and said the cost should not fall on existing taxpayers.

A delegate for developers urged Council to keep the project in 2023. The delegate said the two roads are rural in design with safety concerns and no safe walking or cycling links to schools and community facilities. The delegate also said the project would open up land for a range of housing types.

Staff said the 2023 construction work would be financed by debenture, and that reserves would go negative even apart from Bill 23. Staff also said early tenders were coming in lower than expected, and that developers could front the infrastructure cost under an advanced-timing agreement. Enough funds were already released to finish design.

On the Hawthorne Street proposal, councillors asked about affordable units, the larger density, reduced amenity space and the single entrance. They also asked about the community benefit now that Section 37 agreements are gone. The applicant's planner said community benefits charges would apply and that a fuller urban design review would come at site plan.

On Columbia Street, councillors raised concerns about the number of parking spaces in a walkable area, delivery and rideshare vehicles stopping on the road, and den rooms being converted to bedrooms. Staff and the applicant said enforcement clauses would apply, drop-off spaces could be considered, and the building would be ready for electric vehicle charging.
